# Node drain status API reference

The node drain status endpoints report whether a Terraform Enterprise node is actively running Terraform tasks and whether it is safe to terminate.

## Node status values

Endpoints report one of the following `status` values for each node.

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `ok` | The node is healthy and accepting work. No drain has been initiated. |
| `draining` | A drain has been initiated and the node is still running one or more tasks. The node is not safe to terminate. |
| `standby` | The node has finished draining and is no longer running tasks. The node is safe to terminate. |
| `error` | The drain status could not be determined for this node. `active_tasks_count` is `null` and `active_tasks` is an empty array. |

## Get local node drain status

This endpoint returns the drain status of the individual node that receives the request. Because this endpoint targets the local node, send the request directly to that node instead of through a load balancer. Authentication is required to use this endpoint.

`GET /api/v1/nodes/self/drain-status`

### Sample request

```shell
curl \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --request GET \
  "https://tfe.example.com:8443/api/v1/nodes/self/drain-status"
```

### Sample response

The following response shows a node that has finished draining and is safe to terminate. Because the drain is complete, `status` is `standby`, `is_safe_to_terminate` is `true`, `active_tasks` is empty, both `drain_started_at` and `force_terminate_at` are populated, and `force_terminate_at` is exactly `drain_started_at` plus 24 hours.

```json
{
  "hostname": "tfe-1",
  "status": "standby",
  "is_safe_to_terminate": true,
  "active_tasks_count": 0,
  "active_tasks": [],
  "drain_started_at": "2026-06-09T14:32:00Z",
  "force_terminate_at": "2026-06-10T14:32:00Z"
}
```

When the drain status cannot be determined, `status` is `error`, `active_tasks_count` is `null`, and `active_tasks` is empty. The request still returns `200`.

```json
{
  "hostname": "tfe-1",
  "status": "error",
  "is_safe_to_terminate": false,
  "active_tasks_count": null,
  "active_tasks": []
}
```

### Response codes

| Status | Response | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [200][] | Node drain status object  | Request successful |
| [401][] | [JSON API error object][] | Authentication required |
| [429][] | [JSON API error object][] | Too many requests. Wait before retrying. |
| [500][] | [JSON API error object][] | Internal server error |

## Get cluster drain status

This endpoint returns a collection with the drain status of every node in the Terraform Enterprise deployment, sorted by hostname. It fans the drain status check out to all live nodes and returns one resource per node, so you do not need to query each node individually. A node that cannot be reached still appears in the collection with `status: error`, and the request stays `200`. Use the `filter[nodes]` parameter to scope the collection to specific nodes by hostname. Authentication is required to use this endpoint.

`GET /api/v1/nodes/drain-status`

### Query parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `filter[nodes]` | array of strings | Optional. Restrict the collection to the given node hostnames. Use `tfectl node list` to view node hostnames. If omitted, the response includes all nodes in the deployment. |

### Sample request

```shell
curl \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/vnd.api+json" \
  --request GET \
  "https://tfe.example.com:8443/api/v1/nodes/drain-status?filter[nodes]=tfe-1"
```

### Sample response

The following response includes one node. The node `tfe-1` is `draining` and reports one active `agent-run` task. Each resource's `links.self` is a relative path that scopes the collection to that node.

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "tfe-1",
      "type": "node-drain-status",
      "attributes": {
        "hostname": "tfe-1",
        "status": "draining",
        "is_safe_to_terminate": false,
        "active_tasks_count": 1,
        "active_tasks": [
          {
            "name": "agent-run",
            "started_at": "2026-06-09T14:40:11Z",
            "metadata": {
              "run_id": "run-CkszD4iCEaxnYMkh",
              "workload_id": "plan-pJ5bfP4pFxQVHDkT",
              "workload_type": "Plan",
              "workspace_name": "my-app-prod",
              "organization_name": "acme-corp",
              "organization_id": "org-bright-raven-404724",
              "image_tag": "1.28.8",
              "tfc_address": "https://tfe.example.com",
              "terraform_download_url": "https://releases.hashicorp.com/terraform/1.9.5/terraform_1.9.5_linux_amd64.zip",
              "terraform_checksum": "9f3ca38a6d2a6b1c0f4e3d2c1b0a9988776655443322110aabbccddeeff0011"
            }
          }
        ],
        "drain_started_at": "2026-06-09T14:32:00Z",
        "force_terminate_at": "2026-06-10T14:32:00Z"
      },
      "links": {
        "self": "/api/v1/nodes/drain-status?filter[nodes]=tfe-1"
      }
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "partial": false
  }
}
```

### Collection `meta` block

The top-level document contains a `data` array and a `meta` block. The `meta` block reports whether the snapshot is complete.

| Attribute | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `meta.partial` | boolean | `true` when Terraform Enterprise could not enumerate all intended nodes, such as when the database is unavailable and only the local node could be queried. When `partial` is `true`, the request returns `503`. `false` when the collection reflects every node in the deployment. |
| `meta.warnings` | array of strings | Non-fatal issues encountered during the run, such as the database being unavailable. This field is omitted when there are no warnings. |

### Response codes

| Status | Response | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [200][] | [JSON API document][] | Request successful. Unreachable nodes appear as `error` resources and still return `200`. |
| [400][] | [JSON API error object][] | A `filter[nodes]` entry is blank |
| [401][] | [JSON API error object][] | Authentication required |
| [404][] | [JSON API error object][] | A hostname in `filter[nodes]` does not exist |
| [429][] | [JSON API error object][] | Too many requests. Wait before retrying. |
| [500][] | [JSON API error object][] | Internal server error |
| [503][] | [JSON API document][] | The database is unavailable. The response is partial, with `meta.partial` set to `true`. |

## Response schema

The endpoints describe each node with the same fields. The local endpoint returns these fields at the top level of a flat JSON object, and the cluster endpoint nests them under `attributes` in each `node-drain-status` resource.

| Field | Type | Nullable | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hostname` | string | no | Node hostname. Use `tfectl node list` to view node hostnames. |
| `status` | string enum | no | One of `ok`, `draining`, `standby`, or `error`. |
| `is_safe_to_terminate` | boolean | no | `true` only when `status` is `standby`. |
| `active_tasks_count` | integer | yes | Number of tasks currently executing on the node. `null` when `status` is `error`. |
| `active_tasks` | array of objects | no | Per-task detail. Empty array when the count is `0` or when `status` is `error`. |
| `drain_started_at` | timestamp | yes | When a drain was initiated. Omitted when no drain has been initiated. |
| `force_terminate_at` | timestamp | yes | `drain_started_at` plus 24 hours. Omitted when no drain has been initiated. |

### Per-task fields

Each element of `active_tasks` describes one task that is currently executing on the node. The task-level `name` and `started_at` fields are at the top level of the task object, and the remaining fields are nested under the `metadata` object. Terraform Enterprise omits any `metadata` field that has no value, and it never includes sensitive fields such as tokens.

| Field | Type | Nullable | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | no | Task name. One of `agent-run`, `vcs-ingress`, `sentinel`, `cost-estimation`, or `plan-export-worker`. |
| `started_at` | timestamp | no | When the task began executing. |
| `metadata` | object | no | Per-task metadata. The fields listed below are nested under this object. |
| `metadata.run_id` | string | yes | Present for `agent-run` workspace runs (Plan, Apply, Assessment, TestRun, and TestRunCleanup). Absent for stack runs, `vcs-ingress`, and other types. |
| `metadata.workload_id` | string | yes | Present for all `agent-run` and `vcs-ingress` tasks. Absent for `sentinel`, `cost-estimation`, and `plan-export-worker`. |
| `metadata.workload_type` | string | yes | The type of workload, for example `Apply`, `Stacks::Operations::Plan`, or `SourceBundle`. Populated under the same conditions as `workload_id`. |
| `metadata.workspace_name` | string | yes | Present for `agent-run` workspace runs. Absent otherwise. |
| `metadata.stack_name` | string | yes | Present for `agent-run` stack operations (`Stacks::Operations::Plan` and `Stacks::Operations::Apply`). Absent otherwise. |
| `metadata.organization_name` | string | yes | Present for `agent-run` workspace runs and conditional for stack operations. Absent for `vcs-ingress`. |
| `metadata.organization_id` | string | yes | Present for all `agent-run` and `vcs-ingress` tasks. Absent for `sentinel`, `cost-estimation`, and `plan-export-worker`. |
| `metadata.image_tag` | string | yes | Agent image tag, normalized upstream with any leading colon stripped, for example `1.28.8`. |
| `metadata.tfc_address` | string | yes | The Terraform Enterprise address used for this run. |
| `metadata.terraform_download_url` | string | yes | The Terraform binary download URL. |
| `metadata.terraform_checksum` | string | yes | The Terraform binary checksum. |
| `metadata.payload_url` | string | yes | Present for `sentinel` tasks. |
